name: aromir_repair_vs_probe
purpose: TASKS 73, 216 (the user, 15 Nov: release v1.3 for aromir, step g): aromir's soft-mode repair on D_ac28161d06 (C24H14, 38 atoms) against the probe's patch of 13 Nov (B3LYP lowest mode -7.48 -> +7.05 cm-1, probes/results_m1/low_mode_patch_2026-11-13/corpus/D_ac28161d06/report.json), from the same geometry and the same unpatched label Hessian (corpus/superseded_2026-11-14). The gradient call is aromir's: mf.nuc_grad_method().set(grid_response=True).kernel(), as pyscf's grad/test/test_rks.py; aromir's own estimate for this molecule is about 3.9 GB for one atom's grid (8 x 99 x 590 x (10 nao + 3 natm^2 + 5 natm) bytes, nao 388). Two displaced SCFs and gradients; pyscf's log grows in the result folder's pyscf.log.

estimate.basis: the probe's two B3LYP points of this molecule took 542 s and 545 s with the blocked grid response on the laptop (low_mode_patch_2026-11-13/corpus/D_ac28161d06/b3lyp/dir_0_*.json); pyscf's unblocked gradient and a tighter start are allowed twice that

memory.basis: a bound: probes/wsl_capped.sh stops the run at 10240 MB (CAP_MB; pyscf max_memory 5120, above aromir's 3.9 GB estimate for the gradient); the probe's blocked run of this molecule peaked at 1.84 GB (label_route_vs_probe.log)
